children: Software and cloud computing giant Oracle Corp. (ORCL, Financials) is getting a feel for just how costly the AI boom can be.

But the corporation is shedding employment while spending billions on the data centers needed to keep up with the surging demand for artificial intelligence. Wall Street thus far seems willing to make that trade-off.
Shares of Oracle jumped more than 2% in Thursday premarket trade, adding to gains of around 2% on Wednesday.
The company's staff shrunk by over 21,000, or 13%, during the fiscal year that ended May 31. Another round of layoffs this week.
Those cuts have a cost of their own. Oracle increased its planned restructuring expenditures by $700 million to around $2.8 billion. At the same time, its AI business is booming.
Oracle inked more than $30 billion in new AI cloud contracts recently, boosting the remainder of its performance obligations to $664 billion.
Now it must build up enough infrastructure to meet those contracts.
This puts pressure on cash flow. Data-center spending increased, and free cash flow was about minus $5 billion.
Oracle said certain customers might help by paying up ahead or by providing chips.
The next test is to turn that huge backlog into cash. If it happens soon enough, today's expenditure and job cuts may appear very different in retrospect.

title: Oracle stock rises as investors look past layoffs to its AI backlog
